abstract: Every year, groundbreaking discoveries are born in university labs-potential cures, diagnostics, and life-saving technologies that could transform healthcare as we know it. Yet, too many of these innovations remain untapped, unable to cross the daunting ‘valley of death’. As the complexity and scale of research problems grow, American universities are rapidly evolving to support the continued development of nascent technologies by establishing internal funding and innovator support mechanisms. Recent instability in the major federal funding initiatives, traditionally a substantial and reliable source of funding for very early-stage research and development, further underscores the need for universities to look for new avenues of funding to support translation of discoveries into real-world products, solutions and services. Here we discuss key elements of Rutgers’ approach to building an effective and sustainable university technology commercialization fund, with an emphasis on getting industry input early to improve outcomes in the short and long term.
